Each agent and subagent follows the enabled Graphit modules below.
Match the current action; read its skill immediately before first use. Reuse loaded instructions for the same project/overrides; reload only needed skills after target/overrides change or compaction loses them. Never preload all skills.
Use Graphit MCP before native discovery, including cluster neighbors: their returned `dir` is `project_dir` for target module reads. If a required tool is unavailable, record the limitation and use default native tools; never substitute the Graphit CLI.
Structured MCP results default to TOON text; use top-level `ai_optimized: false` for JSON machine consumers. Root AST Source and SessionHook remain text. Use narrow queries, compact results and selected sources; stop when evidence answers. Reuse fresh evidence; expand for concrete gaps.
Memory: facts/lessons; Task: sessions, analysis/decisions and work state; Knowledge: contracts; AST: code; Hub: cluster-first discovery. New questions at any stage trigger needed recall; reuse sufficient evidence.
`project_dir` is call-local. Persist project identity and relative paths in shared content, never a machine-specific checkout root; resolve it again on each host. Stores follow the checked-out project version (Git branch; `main` without Git); optional `project_version` reaches another.
Persistence boundary for every module: shared project records may contain only non-sensitive content inherent to the project and needed for confirmed contracts, decisions, evidence, operations or technical continuity. Never persist personal or sensitive user/organization data, secrets, credentials, security-risk material, or an engineer's feelings, frustration, transient impressions or unconfirmed speculation. User-only context belongs only in private user memory when it is a durable, legitimately useful preference or correction; otherwise do not persist it. Keep necessary technical hypotheses explicitly labelled and never promote them to facts.
Hooks load mandatory memory and restore routing at lifecycle boundaries. After interruptions, corrections or handoff, resume durable session/task state and revise changed requests before execution.
Never initiate or retry `git push` automatically. Only an explicit engineer request for that push authorizes it; a commit, delivery, or `pre-push` hook does not.
Checkpoint each independently reportable work unit in the active Task and session. Close delivered sessions explicitly. After the final task update, the adapter stop hook requests a PROJECT index rescan asynchronously; do not duplicate it, wait for it, or sync after every edit.
Subagent default: create none unless the user or an applicable mandate, AGENTS.md, loaded skill or higher-priority instruction explicitly assigns bounded work to a delegated role; that instruction authorizes and requires only that role and work. This mandate assigns recall→`graphit-scout`, impact review→`graphit-tracker`, and decided transcription→`graphit-scribe`. A performer already in that role works directly, not recursively. Delegates report evidence and may finish; no waiting loop. The coordinator may later send that delegate another instruction through host follow-up/resume when supported. Reuse is optional: no keep-alive, reuse or explicit dismissal is required, and ending a turn does not complete Graphit work. Acceptance, checkpoints, Task/session claims, revisions, completion and lifecycle stay with the coordinator. If the host cannot run the role, read its agents-directory document and perform only that role yourself.

graphit:
# AST Code Exploration
Before locating/reading code or assessing structure/impact, including before native grep, glob, file reads or symbol navigation, read `installed-graphit-ast` if its instructions are not in the current context; then use its Graphit MCP tools.

graphit:
# Task
Before starting/resuming project work, planning, delegating/completing it, or answering questions and investigating system/history gaps at any stage, read `installed-graphit-task` if its instructions are not in the current context; then use its Graphit MCP tools.
Core tools: `catalog_g__task_session_get`, `catalog_g__task_session_list`, `catalog_g__task_session_create`, `catalog_g__task_session_claim`, `catalog_g__task_get`, `catalog_g__task_query`, `catalog_g__task_create`. The skill routes the remaining tools.
Explicitly send typed references (target type/id and relation) when citing records in writes; prose alone creates no database relation. Read the module skill for scope and update semantics. Read the open sessions and DECIDE by scope, not recency: the same evolving demand continues in its session across interruptions, changed scope revises that session and its affected Tasks, and only a different demand gets a new one. With no match, create a detailed demand/strategy session and claim coordination. Read session.md before its lifecycle actions. Bind every agent-created Task to session_id; workers share it without taking coordination. Investigate before saving specification -> plan -> dependency-ordered Tasks with checks; batch planned packets with known IDs and inspect each result. Install missing commands needed for delivery quality, conformance and tests; persist one Windows/macOS/Linux invocation: project binaries by project-relative path, others via system PATH; never machine paths. A user-requested validation or user-reported missing-validation error makes its project check necessary. Before commit/delivery, put fast necessary checks in pre-commit and long checks in pre-push; verify lockfile hooks and Git activation. `pre-push` is only a gate: never initiate or retry `git push` without an explicit engineer request for that push. Manual runs alone are no gate; inactive hooks stay unresolved. Keep leaves usable without this conversation. Checkpoint progress, problems, decisions, strategy and next action at meaningful outcomes. Recall sessions/Tasks whenever new doubts arise. Handoff preserves state and releases claims; a turn ending is not completion. Close the session explicitly only after linked Tasks are terminal and scope/evidence is reconciled; cancelled work is not delivered.

After an authorized Git commit or amend succeeds, resolve the full commit ID (`git rev-parse HEAD`) and update `Task.commit` on the Tasks whose changes are actually included using `catalog_g__task_commit_set`. This also applies to completed Tasks; preserve their status and check evidence. Never infer a commit from a planned command or treat this instruction as authorization to commit or push.
